data.description:
# Mining laser

## Problem statement

Asteroids are an inert world hazard that drift through the field and drop minerals when destroyed (small asteroids drop one mineral; a large chain is 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 destroys). Mining them competes directly with shooting the actual threats, so mineral farming is a manual detour. Add a **Mining Laser** power-up: a rapid-firing laser that only ever targets asteroids and always fires at the nearest one, so the player can farm minerals passively while keeping their normal weapon trained on enemies.

## Users

- **Player (primary).** Wants minerals for the hold/reward loop without diverting aim from enemies.
- **Game/balance designer.** Wants one clean, data-driven power-up kind with tunable fire rate, damage and duration.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I collect a Mining Laser my ship automatically fires rapid laser shots at the nearest asteroid, so I can farm minerals without stopping my attack on enemies.
- As a player, the Mining Laser never wastes shots on empty space or on enemies — it only fires at a live asteroid.
- As a player, when there are no asteroids, the Mining Laser is silent and does not distract me.

## Resolved decisions (producer answers)

- **D1 — Delivery model.** It is a **normal weapon power-up** that occupies one of the six loadout slots when permanently owned, and it has **upgrade levels** (the standard power-up level curve). It is an additive auxiliary weapon: collecting it does **not** replace the cannon, so the player can still damage enemies.
- **D2 — Acquisition & duration.** It is acquired as a **field pickup** (temporary level, reverts at its TTL, refreshable on re-collect) **and** as a **permanent hold-full reward** that stays owned in a slot and auto-fires for the rest of the run on a level-derived interval — mirroring the Orbital Strike precedent.
- **D3 — Targeting.** It targets the **nearest live asteroid of any size tier**, computed with wrapped distance so an asteroid just across the screen seam (including one currently off-screen) is a valid target. It **never** targets non-asteroid enemies. It retargets immediately to the new nearest asteroid when its current target is destroyed. When no live asteroid exists it fires nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `mining_laser` power-up is present in `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) with a name, player-facing description, drop weight, temporary window and a level spec; it is a normal slot-occupying kind (not exempt at the six-slot cap) and has upgrade levels in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` + `src/data/powerup-levels.json`.
- Collecting a Mining Laser as a **field pickup** makes the ship auto-fire at the **nearest live asteroid** at a rapid beat-grid cadence for its temporary window; re-collecting refreshes the window and the level, and the level reverts to the permanent level (or unowned) when the window expires.
- Taking the **permanent hold-full reward** owns the Mining Laser in a slot and keeps it auto-firing at the nearest live asteroid for the rest of the run, on the level-derived cadence.
- Targeting uses **wrapped distance** so an asteroid across the screen seam (even off-screen) can be the nearest target; a nearer non-asteroid enemy is ignored in favour of an asteroid.
- The Mining Laser **never damages or targets non-asteroid enemies** (scouts, harvesters, boss, etc.).
- When no live asteroid exists, the Mining Laser fires **no shots** (no empty-space or forward-fallback fire).
- When the current target asteroid is destroyed, the Mining Laser retargets to the **new nearest** live asteroid on the next shot, including split children.
- The targeting rule is a pure, shared helper (asteroid-only nearest selection using wrapped distance) consumed by both the game and the gym, with gym↔game parity asserted by the existing duplicate-body/parity guards.
- The Mining Laser is exercised in the appropriate gym scene (mineral/asteroid gym and/or the combat power-up gym) and shares the same core code as `PlayScene`.
- A code-drawn drop icon, catalogue description and HUD/active-effect readout exist, and the drop pool, hold-full choice and gym help surfaces include the new kind consistently.
- Unit tests cover: target selection (only asteroids, nearest with wrap seam, idle when none, retarget on kill/child spawn), cadence/fire path, temporary-window expiry and permanent ownership, and gym↔game parity.
- Documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 power-up table and count) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and any relevant wiki/docs entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can collect a Mining Laser that automatically chews through the nearest asteroids, making mineral farming passive so they can keep firing at enemies.

## Constraints

- Must not fork the power-up, effects, targeting, bullet or HUD seams — reuse the shared core so gym↔game parity holds by construction.
- Must not weaken the existing asteroid-skip rule for Arc/Orbital Strike (`src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`); the Mining Laser is the explicit, documented inverse.
- Must not target enemies, ever — even a nearer enemy must be ignored in favour of an asteroid.
- It is a slot-occupying power-up with upgrade levels, not a cannon-replacing weapon and not a timed hit-and-forget weapon drop.
- Tuning (fire cadence, damage, TTL, drop weight, level curve) is balance data recorded in the work item, not hard-coded behaviour spread across scenes.
- No frame-rate-dependent behaviour; cadence runs on the shared beat/onset grid.

## Existing state

- Power-ups are a 16-kind catalogue (`PowerUpId`) with a permanent/temporary level split, timed/instant windows, a shared `EffectsRegistry`, level specs in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` and data in `src/data/powerup-levels.json`; a run's loadout is capped at six permanent slots.
- Auto-firing power-ups already exist: the **Orbital Strike** (`strike`) fires a bolt at the nearest live **non-asteroid** enemy on a level-derived interval (`selectOrbitalStrikeTarget`, `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`); the **Mystery UFO** spawns a drone that seeks the nearest mineral.
- Auto-targeting eligibility is centralised in the pure `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` (`isEligibleAutoTarget` / `isInertWorldHazard`), which *excludes* the `asteroid` archetype for Arc and Orbital Strike.
- Asteroids are `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` (archetype `'asteroid'`, 1 HP, three tiers, four-edge screen wrap). Small-asteroid mineral drops are resolved by `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` / `asteroidKillDrops.ts`.
- The shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, `CombatScene.ts`) owns `_autoFire`, the beat clock and all power-up pulse/consumption steps; gym scenes inherit it.

## Desired change

Add a Mining Laser power-up kind whose auto-fire is an **asteroid-targeting** sibling of the Orbital Strike: a pure nearest-live-asteroid selector (wrapped distance, any tier), a shared core fire step that emits rapid laser shots at the target, permanent-slot and level-curve wiring, icon/HUD/drop wiring, and gym coverage — with the crystal-clear rule that it only ever fires at asteroids and is silent when none exist.

**Key Files:** (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add `'mining_laser'` to `PowerUpId` and a `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry (name, description, drop weight, `temporaryWindow`, slot-occupying/consumable flags as appropriate).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` + `src/data/powerup-levels.json` — level spec (fire cadence, damage, temporary window, slot behaviour).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — per-run/pending state and the consume/resolve seam for the shared combat core.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared `_updateMiningLaser` step (target → fire on cadence), consuming the level store.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — resolve a fired shot against the asteroid through the shared damage path.
- New pure helper (e.g. `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.ts` or an extension of `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`) — nearest-live-asteroid selector using wrapped distance.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` / `src/scenes/core/` bullet or hitscan seam — reuse the shared player-bullet path.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — default drop weight / drop-pool inclusion.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts`, `src/powerups/dropDescriptions.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts` — icon, description, slot integration, readout.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` (and/or `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`) — gym coverage and parity.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — documentation.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.*.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/*.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts`, gym parity tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Target-selection edge cases.** Asteroids wrap at the screen seam; "nearest" must use wrapped distance (as `findNearestTarget` / `selectOrbitalStrikeTarget` do) so a target just across the seam — or off-screen across it — is chosen correctly.
- **Split chains.** Destroying a large/medium asteroid spawns children; the laser must retarget to a child (if still nearest) or another asteroid without firing into empty space.
- **Slot interaction.** It takes a permanent slot when owned and is not slot-cap-exempt; verify the hold-full choice gating and mini-boss wheel behave correctly at six owned slots.
- **Balance risk.** A rapidly auto-firing laser makes mineral farming near-passive; drop weight, cadence, damage and TTL should be tuned (start from Orbital Strike/Extra Life rarity precedents) and recorded.
- **Parity risk.** If any scene copies the fire logic instead of consuming the shared core, the duplicate-body guard/parity test will fail — implement once in the shared core.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Do **not** also add asteroid targeting to other weapons or add mining-laser variants; record such ideas as separate linked work items.

## Related work

- **Orbital Strike power-up (AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — nearest-target auto-firing power-up precedent (`strike`, `selectOrbitalStrikeTarget`, level-derived interval, field vs permanent).
- **Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69)** — the auto-target asteroid-skip rule the Mining Laser deliberately inverts.
- **Shared auto-target eligibility rule (AH-0MVVHAAUJ0080M9M / AH-0MVVHAD7Z005X5UW)** — `isEligibleAutoTarget` / `isInertWorldHazard`.
- **Asteroids drop collectable minerals (AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q)** and the shared mineral kill-drop helper (AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB) — the mineral economy the laser feeds.
- **Gym minerals / asteroid gym** (`src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`) — natural observation scene.
- **Power-up catalogue + effects (epic AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z / AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — catalogue/level conventions.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery model.** Should the Mining Laser fire **alongside** the player's normal weapon (player can still shoot enemies), or is it acceptable for it to **replace** the main weapon while active? Options: (a) auxiliary/additive; (b) cannon-replacing. — **Recommended:** (a) auxiliary — a cannon-replacing weapon that can only hit asteroids would leave the player unable to damage enemies. **Answer (producer):** "It's a normal weapon power up that takes one of the slots available, with upgrade levels." → Resolved as an **additive, slot-occupying power-up with upgrade levels** (does not replace the cannon). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Acquisition & duration.** How should it be acquired? Options: (a) field pickup only, timed (~15 s) and refreshable; (b) field pickup **and** a permanent hold-full reward that repeats on a level-derived interval (Orbital Strike precedent); (c) permanent once collected. — **Recommended:** (b). **Answer (producer):** **B** — field pickup **and** permanent hold-full reward repeating on a level-derived interval. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — No-asteroid behaviour & asteroid tiers.** When no asteroid is present, should it be silent, and which asteroids are eligible? Options: (a) idle unless a live on-screen asteroid exists; target nearest any-tier asteroid; retarget on kill; (b) idle, but also consider off-screen asteroids across the wrap seam; (c) always fire forward when none exists. — **Recommended:** (a). **Answer (producer):** **B** — idle when none exists, but target the nearest live asteroid using **wrapped distance**, including asteroids across the screen seam / off-screen; nearest any-tier asteroid; retarget on kill. Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV5CB6KO0079N08** – Remove the Power Pellet power-up from the game (completed)
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)
- **AH-0MVU3341U001B40T** – Orbital Strike must not target asteroids (producer rejection remediation) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mubvgi62004ed9q, 0muhmt5jc004wrsb, 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvnsig1o0049g69, acceptance (+406 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, acceptance, active, actual, add (+387 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvnsig1o0049g69, acceptance, active, actual (+359 more)

## Plan (2026-11-09)

Decomposed into seven features, created in **test-first / dependency order**. Every phase is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs where the slice needs them), and each is a separate worktree/session.

| Phase | Feature | Depends on | Effort / risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Mining-laser target rule (asteroid-only, wrapped) — AH-0MW9QMMOT0014IU0 | — | S / Low |
| F2 | Mining-laser catalogue kind and level curve — AH-0MW9QMNYP006ZO6T | — | S / Medium |
| F3 | Shared core mining-laser fire step — AH-0MW9QMP2P0032BWW | F1, F2 | M / High |
| F4 | Mining-laser beam VFX and audio cue — AH-0MW9QMQ7B005WFH9 | F3 | S / Low |
| F5 | Mining-laser surfaces: icon, description, drop, HUD — AH-0MW9QMRC7007HVHQ | F2 | S / Medium |
| F6 | Gym coverage and parity for the mining laser — AH-0MW9QMSI7005UU9P | F3, F5 | M / Medium |
| F7 | Docs: GDD §4.4, balancing, GYM_PARITY and guards — AH-0MW9QMTWL0075S32 | F5, F6 | XS / Low |

Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated with anything the previous phase learned (tuning values, helper names, VFX colour).

### Corrections to the predicted Key Files (facts, not intent)

- **`src/data/powerup-levels.json` does not exist.** The `src/data` parity JSONs are weapon-only (`weapon-levels.json`, `weapon-levels-parity.json`). Power-up level data lives solely in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, so the AC's "+ JSON" clause is satisfied by that module alone. No new JSON file is invented unless a separate parity-file capability is requested.
- **`src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` is not the fire seam.** The laser resolves as an **instant beam** (see Recorded assumptions), so it reuses `CombatScene.damageEnemyViaAoe` (the shared kill seam) plus a new `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts`, mirroring the `strike` precedent (`vfx/orbitalStrike.ts`). No change to the player-bullet path is needed.
- The targeting helper is `src/scenes/core/miningLaserTargeting.ts` (the first, not the second, predicted option) and reuses `findNearestTarget` + `wrappedDistance` rather than re-implementing nearest selection.

### Recorded assumptions (correctable at review, not blocking)

1. **Instant beam, not a travelling projectile.** A projectile can collide with a non-asteroid enemy in flight, which the "never damages enemies" AC forbids; an instant resolve damages only the selected asteroid. A hitscan beam also works in gyms whose formation config collects no bullets (`GymMinerals` has `collectBullets: () => []`).
2. **No latched/banked shots.** Unlike the Orbital Strike (which latches a decided bolt so a pickup is never wasted), a cadence tick with no asteroid is simply skipped — silence is the required behaviour, and there is no single consumable to waste.
3. **Provisional balance values** (all catalogue/level data, retunable without code): cadence base **4 sixteenth-note steps = 750 ms**, −1 step per level, floor **1 step = 187.5 ms**; damage **1 → 2** whole hits (inert today — every asteroid tier is 1 HP); field TTL **10 s** (weapon-window precedent); drop weight **2** (Orbital Strike / Smart Bomb rarity).
4. **Slot behaviour:** a normal slot-counted kind — not `availableWhenSlotsFull`, not `fieldPickupOnly`, not `consumable`; rewarded when owned (level-up offer + mini-boss wedge).
5. **Gym coverage uses both observation scenes:** `GymMinerals` (asteroids only, currently no drop layer → opt in with a mining-laser-only spawner) shows the laser cutting, splitting and paying minerals; `GymPowerUpsCombat` (scouts only) shows the silence rule.
6. **The fire step lives in the shared core** and is called from `_tickPlayer` beside `_updateOrbitalStrike`, so `PlayScene` and every gym run identical code (the duplicate-body guard enforces it).

### OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking — defaults above are recorded so implementation can proceed)

- **Balance sign-off (game/balance designer).** Are the provisional cadence (0.75 s → 0.1875 s), damage (1 → 2), field TTL (10 s) and drop weight (2) the intended starting point, or should the laser be rarer/slower because passive farming is strong? The values are data; changing them later is a one-file edit in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` + `src/core/rules.ts`.
- **Feel (producer).** Instant beam vs travelling laser bolts. The instant beam is chosen for the "never damages enemies" guarantee and is the shipped default; a bolt look would need an asteroid-only collision filter and a parity test.
- **Damage axis.** Keep `miningLaserDamage` even though every asteroid is 1 HP today (catalogue-consistency), or drop the axis and make cadence the only level curve?

### Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (continued)

- **Q4 — Level-data location.** The AC names `src/data/powerup-levels.json`; no such file exists and the `src/data` parity files are weapon-only. **Answer (agent, from repository inspection):** level data lives in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` only; the AC is satisfied there and no JSON is invented. Evidence: `ls src/data` (no powerup file), `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`. Recorded as an AC-scope correction above.
- **Q5 — Fire delivery (beam vs projectile) for this codebase.** Auto-targeting offence's asteroid rule lives in `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` (skip asteroids) and the strike's selector in `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`. **Answer (agent, research):** add the explicit inverse predicate + a sibling selector that reuses `findNearestTarget(..., world)`; resolve fire instantly through `damageEnemyViaAoe`, matching the `strike` VFX seam (`src/vfx/orbitalStrike.ts`). Proposed to the producer as the non-blocking "feel" OPEN QUESTION above.
- **Q6 — Where can the behaviour be observed?** `GymMinerals` (`src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts`) is asteroids-only but has **no** field-drop layer; `GymPowerUpsCombat` cycles power-ups but fields scouts only. **Answer (agent, research):** opt `GymMinerals` into the existing shared `powerUps` layer config with a mining-laser-only spawner, and add the kind to the combat gym's cycle — both consume the shared core, no gym fork. Recorded as F6.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-09 — Initial decomposition (F1–F7) created, dependency edges wired (F3←F1,F2; F4←F3; F5←F2; F6←F3,F5; F7←F5,F6), predicted-Key-Files corrections and recorded balance assumptions appended, three non-blocking open questions recorded.

# Extra Life adaptive probabilities — Intake Brief (AH-0MW8178ZR0090CNY)

## Original request (verbatim)

> Create a minor increase in the probabiliyt of an extra life power up being dropped as the player loses lives. It should not be noticable, but the player should "feel lucky" when one drops and they are low on lives. This, presumably means the amount of increase is exponential as the player drops to only 1 life left. Also ensure that a mini-boss kill *always* leaves an extra life power up.

> **Producer answers received (this intake):** Q1 → **(a)** scale the
> `extra_life` weight in the existing weighted pool; Q2 → **(a)** always spawn
> a physical `extra_life` field pickup at the death position, in addition to the
> wheel reward, even at the life cap / full slots; Q3 → a **gentler curve than
> the offered (b): `1× / 2× / 4×` at `3 / 2 / 1` lives** (i.e. a multiplier of
> **`2^livesLost`**). Asteroid clarification: small asteroids **no longer drop
> lives** at shipped defaults — see "Existing state" below.

## Problem statement

Extra Life currently drops at one fixed rate for the whole run, regardless of
how many lives the player has left. A player down to their last life therefore
gets no extra recovery help, and the moment an Extra Life appears never feels
like a lucky break. Separately, defeating a bespoke mini-boss — the biggest
scheduled highlight of every level — never leaves a life on the field, so the
encounter has no guaranteed survivability payoff.

## Users

- **Players** — want a subtle, invisible-to-them safety net that makes an Extra
  Life feel like a lucky break exactly when they are low on lives, and want a
  mini-boss kill to reliably restore a life.
- **Designers / balance tuners** — need the adaptive curve and the mini-boss
  guarantee expressed as named, persisted tunables (not scattered magic
  numbers) so the feel can be retuned without code changes.
- **Developers / AI agents** — need the rule defined once in the shared core so
  the game and every gym cannot drift apart (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a **player on my last life**, I want an Extra Life to drop a little more
  often than usual, so I get a genuine chance to turn a doomed run around —
  without ever noticing the game is helping me.
- As a **player who just beat a mini-boss**, I want the wreck to always leave
  an Extra Life, so the hardest fight in the level reliably pays back a life.
- As a **designer**, I want the adaptive curve in one tunable place so I can
  soften or sharpen the "lucky" feeling without touching gameplay code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Adaptive mechanism (one shared rule):** Extra Life drop
      propensity scales with the player's remaining lives by scaling the
      `extra_life` **weight inside the existing weighted per-kill drop pool**
      (the total per-kill drop chance is unchanged; Extra Life simply becomes a
      larger share of the drops that do occur). The multiplier is exactly
      `1×` at or above the run's starting lives and is monotonically
      non-decreasing as lives fall. The rule lives once in a shared pure helper
      consumed by both `PlayScene` and every drop-bearing gym.
- [ ] **AC2 — Curve is `1× / 2× / 4×` at `3 / 2 / 1` lives:** the multiplier is
      `2 ** livesLost`, where `livesLost = max(0, runStartingLives − lives)`
      (`runStartingLives` defaults to 3; a hangar deployment may override it).
      So `≥3` lives → `1×`, `2` lives → `2×`, `1` life → `4×` (and `3` lives
      per the formula). The multiplier is applied to the weight; because the
      weighted pool is normalised, the resulting *probability* uplift is
      slightly below the weight ratio — an intentional extra layer of
      subtlety. At 2 lives the increase is modest ("not noticeable"); at 1 life
      it is a clear but still small uplift.
- [ ] **AC3 — Statistically verifiable:** a seeded simulation (N ≥ 10 000
      representative kills per lives value, documented seed set) demonstrates
      that the Extra Life drop rate at 2 lives and 1 life strictly exceeds the
      full-lives baseline and follows the documented weight-multiplier curve
      within tolerance; the test does not depend on a single lucky seed.
- [ ] **AC4 — Mini-boss always drops one:** every mini-boss defeat spawns
      exactly one `extra_life` **field pickup** at/near the mini-boss death
      position, **in addition to** the existing spin-the-wheel reward, in
      `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss`. It spawns even at the 5-life cap and with a
      full slot pool; the normal drop separation nudge applies, and the existing
      six-slot collection gate and 5-life cap still govern pickup (a drop at the
      cap is simply not useful, but is still spawned).
- [ ] **AC5 — Tunables + persistence:** the curve constant (exponential base,
      default 2) and the starting-lives reference live in `GameRules` with
      documented defaults, clamped on load, and older rules blobs load
      unchanged. The adaptive multiplier composes with the existing level
      scaling (`powerUpDropChance` / `extraLifeDropChance`) and is applied after
      it, so the curve can never rise with campaign level.
- [ ] **AC6 — Parity & no duplicate implementation:** the rule exists once in a
      shared module and is consumed by the game and the gyms (including
      `GymMiniBoss` for the guaranteed drop); the repo-wide duplicate-body guard
      (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests:** unit tests cover the curve (`1×` at full lives,
      `2×` at 2, `4×` at 1, monotonic, clamping/guards), the mini-boss guarantee
      (exactly one `extra_life` spawned per defeat, game + gym), and the seeded
      distribution; the changed-scope test gate passes.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** the GDD §4.4 (Extra Life drop), §3.3.1 / §4.4.4
      (mini-boss defeat/reward — which today state the sweep is cosmetic and the
      wheel is the single reward), the game-rules documentation and code
      comments are updated, including any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who is down to their last life quietly sees Extra Life drops a little
more often — enough to feel lucky, never enough to notice — and every mini-boss
kill now reliably leaves one on the field.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (`AGENTS.md`; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`): the rule
  lives once in the shared core and is consumed by `PlayScene` and the relevant
  gym scenes (`GymFormationScene`, `GymMiniBoss`, and any asteroid/level gym
  that rolls Extra Life). No divergent copies.
- **Subtlety is a hard requirement:** the curve must not make Extra Life
  common; the player must not be able to perceive the manipulation.
- **No new art/assets:** reuse the existing `extra_life` code-drawn icon and
  shared drop pipeline.
- **Do not regress the deliberate supply reduction:** AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR /
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM halved the supply dial and turned the asteroid
  Extra-Life roll off. The adaptive uplift must be layered on top, not undo
  that tuning.
- **Extra Life stays field-pickup-only:** it must not leak back onto the
  hold-full choice or the mini-boss wheel (§4.4.4). The guaranteed mini-boss
  drop is a field pickup, not a wheel wedge.

## Existing state

- **Generic per-kill drop:** `PlayScene._maybeDropPowerUp()` rolls the
  level-resolved per-kill chance `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)` (0.09 at
  level 1 → 0.025 at level 10), then draws one kind from the shared weighted
  pool via `_drawNextDrop` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`,
  `CombatCoreScene._buildDefaultDropSpawner`). The spawner is built once at
  scene start with fixed weights; there is no per-kill weight adjustment today.
- **Extra Life weight:** fixed `DEFAULT_EXTRA_LIFE_WEIGHT = 3` in
  `src/core/rules.ts` (`defaultPowerUpWeights()`), against 4 for standard
  power-ups and 2 for the rare Smart Bomb / Orbital Strike. It never varies
  with lives.
- **Lives:** `GameState.lives` (start 3, cap `MAX_LIVES = 5` from the Extra
  Life catalogue entry). `Player`/HUD read the same value; the scene has
  `this.gameState.lives` at kill time.
- **Asteroid Extra Life roll — currently OFF:** `rollAsteroidExtraLife` +
  `extraLifeDropChance(level, rules)` in `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`
  is **disabled at shipped defaults**
  (`DEFAULT_ASTEROID_EXTRA_LIFE_DROP_CHANCE = 0`, set by AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR /
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM). **So no, asteroids no longer drop lives.** The rule, the
  `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` key and its clamping/persistence are retained
  so a designer can re-enable the roll with one config value; when they do, the
  adaptive multiplier defined here composes with it (at the default `0` there is
  no behaviour change).
- **Mini-boss defeat:** `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` → `miniBoss.destroy()` runs
  the cosmetic death sweep (no drops, no score, no telemetry) and opens the
  spin-the-wheel reward (§4.4.4). Extra Life is deliberately excluded from the
  wheel. Consequently a mini-boss kill currently leaves **no** Extra Life.
- **Gym consumers:** `GymFormationScene` (`_rollExtraLifeDrop`), `GymLevel`,
  `GymMiniBoss` — the first two already call the shared asteroid roll; the
  mini-boss gym exercises the reward wheel.

## Desired change

1. Add a shared, pure **life-adaptive Extra Life weight multiplier**
   (`2 ** livesLost`, clipped to `≥ 1` and `1×` at/above the run's starting
   lives) and apply it to the `extra_life` weight in the shared weighted
   per-kill drop draw. At full lives the behaviour is byte-for-byte today's; at
   2 lives the likelihood doubles and at 1 life it quadruples, so the player
   "feels lucky" at 1 life without noticing at 2.
2. Make **every mini-boss defeat always spawn one `extra_life` field pickup**
   at/near the death position, on top of the wheel reward, in `PlayScene` and
   `GymMiniBoss`, regardless of the life cap or slot occupancy.
3. Express the curve as named, persisted `GameRules` tunables with documented
   defaults and load-time clamping.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/rules.ts` — add the adaptive-curve tunable (exponential base,
  default 2; starting-lives reference) to `GameRules`, defaults, clamping,
  schema-compatible load.
- `src/core/livesScaling.ts` **(new)** — the pure life→weight-multiplier helper
  (single source of truth), beside `levelScaling.ts`.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — expose the
  Extra-Life weight adjustment through the shared drop draw so game + gyms
  share it (e.g. set the `extra_life` weight before each draw).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — apply the multiplier at kill time
  (`_maybeDropPowerUp`) and spawn the guaranteed Extra Life on mini-boss defeat
  (`_damageMiniBoss` / `_finaliseMiniBossDefeat`).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — consume the shared multiplier
  (full-lives baseline in a gym with no run).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — consume the guaranteed mini-boss drop
  (gym has no run lives: unconditional, matching the game's "always").
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/core/livesScaling.test.ts` **(new)**,
  `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.miniboss*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 / §3.3.1 / §4.4.4 wording.

## Related work

- **Add an extra life power up (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3)** — introduced P8 Extra
  Life (passive +1, cap 5, rarer than standard drops). Completed.
- **Asteroids drop more lives (AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S)** — added the small-asteroid
  Extra-Life roll (`rollAsteroidExtraLife`, `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`),
  later turned off by AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM. Completed.
- **Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene
  (AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X)** — wired `powerUpDropChance` / `extraLifeDropChance`
  into the kill path. Completed.
- **Level-scaling curves (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X)** — `src/core/levelScaling.ts`,
  the supply dial this feature composes with.
- **Supply-dial reduction / asteroid roll off (AH-0MW3MLTY3005MIXR,
  AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM)** — deliberate supply tightening; do not undo.
- **Mini-boss defeat sweep (AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z)** — cosmetic sweep, no drops.
- **Mini-Boss Reward — Spin the Wheel (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)** — the encounter's
  current single reward; Extra Life is field-pickup-only and excluded from the
  wheel. The guaranteed drop in this item must not change that exclusion.
- **Bot prioritises extra lives (AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4)** — the demo brain already
  prefers a live Extra Life pickup below the cap; unaffected but retested.
- **Duplicate check:** no completed item satisfies this brief's ACs. The
  closest completed items (above) implement fixed-rate Extra Life drops and the
  mini-boss reward; neither adapts the rate to lives nor guarantees a
  mini-boss Extra Life. No duplicate found.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Perceptibility risk (highest):** a curve tuned too high is noticeable and
  undermines the "not noticeable" requirement. The chosen `1×/2×/4×` curve is
  deliberately gentle; verify with a seeded statistical test and keep the base
  in `GameRules` for retuning.
- **Compounding with level scaling:** the supply dial already lowers drop
  chance with campaign level. The adaptive multiplier is applied after level
  scaling so a late-campaign player on 1 life still gets the intended uplift.
- **Weight vs probability:** the multiplier scales the *weight*, so the
  resulting probability uplift is slightly below the weight ratio because the
  pool normalises. This is intentional subtlety; the statistical test asserts
  the resulting *probability* ordering, not just the weight.
- **Mini-boss drop at the cap:** a guaranteed drop at 5 lives or with a full
  slot pool may be useless. Producer answer Q2(a): **still spawn it** —
  "always" is literal; the six-slot gate and life cap handle collection.
- **Gym semantics:** gyms have no run lives. `GymMiniBoss` always spawns the
  guaranteed drop; the adaptive multiplier uses the catalogue starting lives
  (3) as the baseline in gyms, so parity tests are deterministic.
- **Asteroid roll is off:** the multiplier's composition with the asteroid roll
  has no visible effect at the shipped default (`0`); it is defined for
  consistency if a designer re-enables the roll.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not add a HUD "pity counter", a visible luck meter,
  or extra-life bounties here — record any such idea as a linked work item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which drop channel should adapt? (mechanism)**
  - (a) Scale the `extra_life` **weight inside the existing weighted per-kill
    pool** (drop frequency unchanged; Extra Life becomes a larger share of the
    existing drops as lives fall).
  - (b) Add a separate independent Extra Life roll per kill.
  - (c) Raise the overall per-kill drop chance when low on lives.
  - **Answer (producer): (a).** Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2 — What does "mini-boss kill always leaves an extra life power up" mean
  exactly?**
  - (a) Always spawn a physical `extra_life` **field pickup** at the death
    position, in addition to the wheel reward, even at the cap / full slots.
  - (b) Same, but only when below the life cap.
  - (c) Add Extra Life as a wheel wedge/outcome instead of a field pickup.
  - **Answer (producer): (a).** Source: interactive reply.

- **Q3 — Curve shape, magnitude, and interaction with level scaling.**
  - (a) `multiplier = base ** livesLost` (base ≈ 2.5–3 offered).
  - (b) A gentler/other curve or a per-lives table (e.g. `1× / 2× / 5×`).
  - (c) Also compose the multiplier into the asteroid Extra-Life roll.
  - **Answer (producer): an even gentler curve than (b) — `1× / 2× / 4×` at
    `3 / 2 / 1` lives.** This is exactly `multiplier = 2 ** livesLost`. For
    (c), the producer's follow-up question ("Asteroids no longer drop lives, do
    they?") was answered: the asteroid Extra-Life roll is **off at shipped
    defaults** (`0`), so there is no live asteroid source today; the shared
    multiplier is nonetheless defined once and applied to every Extra Life
    source so it composes if the roll is re-enabled (no behaviour change at
    `0`). Source: interactive reply + repository inspection
    (`src/core/rules.ts:341`, `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X** – Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene (completed)
- **AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4** – Bot prioritises extra lives in hold-full choice and on-screen pickups (completed)
- **AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3** – Add an extra life power up (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv03gxzq00801t4, 0mv6m2m9p0078n4s, 0mvlisu03006wdod, 0mvofgb6k003yd0z, 0mw10zvlh005ijrm (+499 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv6m2m9p0078n4s, 0mw10zvlh005ijrm, able, ac1, ac2 (+469 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mv6m2m9p0078n4s, 0mvofgb6k003yd0z, 0mw10zvlh005ijrm, able, ac1 (+427 more)

# Manual upgrade of power-ups in the power-up levelling gym

## Problem statement

The power-up levelling gym can only raise a power-up's level by physically collecting a drop or resolving a hold-full permanent grant, so an operator cannot drive an arbitrary kind to an arbitrary level to inspect its curve. This item adds a per-power-up **Assign** button to the gym's existing readout panel so a maintainer can add or level up any power-up directly, mirroring the game's permanent-grant semantics.

## Users

- **Maintainer / designer tuning power-up curves** — wants to push any single power-up through its levels without flying around collecting drops, so the resolver-derived stats readout can be inspected at each step.
- **QA / capture author** — wants a reproducible way to reach a given level state for a screenshot or parity capture.

Example user stories:

- As a maintainer, I click **Assign** on the Shield row so the ship owns Shield at base level, then click again to raise its level and watch the Shield recharge stat fall in the readout.
- As a maintainer, when all six loadout slots are full and I assign a new power-up, the gym drops one of my current slot-counted power-ups at random (losing its levels) so the new kind can be added.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The readout panel (`gym-powerup-level-readout`) renders one native **Assign** button per power-up row, queryable by `data-powerup-assign="<id>"`, and the readout (`getReadout()`) plus every row update immediately after each assignment or removal — all state still read from `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, with no second counter.
2. Clicking **Assign** for a power-up the ship does **not** own adds that kind at base level (no extra level-up on the first assignment); clicking it for one the ship **already** owns raises its permanent level by one — both routed through the shared `grantPermanentPowerUp` seam, so a non-consumable gains a permanent level and a consumable (Shield, Thorn Field, Phase Shift, Teleport, Force Field, Mystery UFO) follows the existing hold-full rule and gains one clamped charge instead.
3. When the loadout is full (`resolvePlayerSlotState(...).isFull`, six slot-counted kinds) and the assigned kind is **not** owned, exactly one slot-counted power-up is removed before the new kind is added, and the removed kind loses its whole state (permanent level, temporary stacks and consumable charges/pool) so its slot genuinely frees.
4. The random victim is drawn only from `slotCountedHeldIds` (slot-exempt Extra Life / Mystery UFO are never victims) via the gym's seeded `sceneRng()`, so a seeded capture reproduces the same victim.
5. An **Assign** button is disabled (a click is a no-op) when at its cap: a non-consumable when every one of its **discrete** curve variables has reached its `cap` (a power-up with no discrete variables is never disabled), and a consumable when its level-derived charge pool is full or a single-use kind already holds its ready activation.
6. Automated tests in `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` cover: first-assign adds at base; repeat-assign levels a non-consumable and grants a charge for a consumable; full-loadout assign removes exactly one slot-counted kind and adds the new one; the removal is seeded/deterministic and never picks an exempt kind; removal clears temporary/charge state; and the disabled-at-cap behaviour for both a discrete-capped and a consumable-capped kind.
7. The gym-only affordance and its rationale are recorded in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and all related documentation is updated (code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries); the gym↔game parity invariants still hold.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A maintainer can now drive any power-up to any level from the levelling gym's readout panel with one click, without collecting drops, and the ship's six-slot loadout is respected automatically.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).** The Assign button is a gym-only *manual control*; it must reuse the shared permanent-grant and level-model seams (`grantPermanentPowerUp`, `PowerUpLevelStore`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `resolvePlayerSlotState`) rather than a divergent copy. The shipped `PlayScene` gains no manual control.
- **Single level model.** No second counter for levels, charges or ownership. The readout already reads only from the store; the new control must write only through the store.
- **Consumable rule is authoritative.** A permanent grant to a consumable adds a charge and never a level (`AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW` AC1); the Assign button must not bypass that for consumables (Q6 = B).
- **Determinism.** Random victim selection must use the gym's seeded `sceneRng()` so scripted captures stay reproducible (`AH-0MVRMHYJR000Y9H8`).
- **No new store-level special-casing in scenes.** Any kind-removal seam belongs on `PowerUpLevelStore` (and a thin `Player` wrapper) so other consumers could reuse it without copying the clear logic.

## Existing state

- `GymPowerUpLeveling` (`src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`) builds a plain-DOM readout panel `#gym-powerup-level-readout` with one `.gym-powerup-level-row` per id in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_IDS`; each row currently holds a label span (`data-powerup-label`) and a stats span (`data-powerup-stats`), wrapped by `makeCollapsible` into a collapsible `gym-panel`.
- Levels are raised only by (a) collecting a drop through `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` and (b) the hold-full `MineralChoiceScene` reward applied via `applyMineralChoiceReward` → `grantPermanentPowerUp`.
- `PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) is the single run-scoped level model: `_permanentGrants`, `_tempStacks`, `_charges`, `_owned`, plus `setPermanentLevel`, `clearTemporary` and `reset`. There is **no** per-kind removal seam today — `setPermanentLevel(id, 0)` drops the permanent grant but leaves the `_owned` flag and any charges behind.
- `resolvePlayerSlotState` / `slotCountedHeldIds` (`src/powerups/slots.ts`) already resolve the six-slot occupancy (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`) and the slot-counted held kinds; Extra Life and Mystery UFO are `availableWhenSlotsFull` (exempt) and `reset` is slot-exempt.
- The curve is asymptotic (`resolvePowerUpAtLevel` documents "levels are unbounded above"); discrete variables flatten exactly at `cap`, continuous variables only approach it.

## Desired change

Per-row **Assign** button in the readout panel:

- Not owned → add the kind at base level via `grantPermanentPowerUp(id, effectsRegistry)` (consumables become owned; repeat clicks then follow the shared charge rule).
- Owned → `grantPermanentPowerUp(id, effectsRegistry)` again (permanent level +1 for a non-consumable, one clamped charge for a consumable).
- Loadout full **and** kind not owned → remove one random slot-counted kind (seeded `sceneRng()`, whole-kind clear) and then add the assigned kind.
- Disabled at cap per AC5.

Add a whole-kind removal seam on the store (e.g. `PowerUpLevelStore.remove(id)` clearing `_permanentGrants`, `_tempStacks`, `_charges`, and `_owned` for that id) plus a thin `Player.removePowerUp(id)` delegate, and reuse the existing shared seams for everything else.

## Plan (plan skill)

**Decision: single vertical slice — no child work items.** The item is one
coherent feature (a gym-only control over the existing store/level seams), has
measurable ACs and a minimal implementation sketch, and is not an epic. Splitting
it into store / UI / tests children would be a horizontal-layer decomposition,
which the skill's vertical-slice rule forbids, so the work stays in one
`implement` slice with the tests written first (AC6) and the docs update (AC7)
in the same change. Effort S (expected 13.5 h, recommended 20 h), risk Medium.

**Review stages applied to the existing content:**

1. Requirements & AC alignment — ACs 1–8 trace to the Problem statement, the
   producer answers (Q1–Q11) and the Constraints; no invented ACs. Corrected
   three stale cross-references ("Disabled at cap per AC6" → AC5,
   "tests covering AC9" → AC6, "AC4/AC9 require the whole-kind clear" →
   AC3/AC6), which pointed at the wrong AC numbers.
2. Completeness — required sections present; `## Key Files (predicted)` paths are
   syntactically valid (each has a path separator and an extension); added the
   two reuse candidates found while verifying (`GymRechargeTuning.ts`,
   `sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts`).
3. Sequencing & dependencies — no children to order; within the slice the
   `PowerUpLevelStore.remove(id)` seam and its unit tests precede the button
   wiring (AC6 tests written first).
4. Scope sizing — one deliverable increment; out-of-scope extras (undo, bulk
   levelling) stay recorded under Risks as follow-ups.
5. Acceptance & testability — every AC is pass/fail via
   `GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`, the store unit tests, `getReadout()` and the
   parity docs assertion.
6. Polish & handoff — description is copy-pasteable for `implement`; verified
   against the live code that no `PowerUpLevelStore.remove`/`Player.removePowerUp`
   seam exists yet and that `grantPermanentPowerUp`, `consumableChargeCap`,
   `hasSingleUse`, `resolvePlayerSlotState` and `slotCountedHeldIds` all exist as
   referenced.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — build the per-row Assign button in `_buildReadoutPanel`, wire its click handler, implement add/level/remove/disable logic against the shared store; add test seams (e.g. a public `assignPowerUp(id)` method the button calls).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — new `PowerUpLevelStore.remove(id)` whole-kind clear (permanent + temporary + charges + owned); a small helper to report whether a kind is at its curve/consumable cap if one does not already exist.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — thin `removePowerUp(id)` delegating to the store (keeps the "player owns the one store" boundary).
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` — reuse `grantPermanentPowerUp` for the assign path; no new reward logic.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — reuse `resolvePlayerSlotState` / `slotCountedHeldIds` for the full check and the random victim pool.
- `src/style.css` — styling for the per-row Assign button and its disabled state (consistent with the `gym-panel` and `gym-panel-toggle` styles).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — tests covering AC6.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — record the gym-only manual assign affordance and its rationale (row in the parity matrix + divergence note).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.ts` — existing gym precedent for calling
  `grantPermanentPowerUp(id, effectsRegistry)` directly from `create()`; reuse
  the same call shape for the Assign seam.
- `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts` — shared six-slot loadout fixtures
  (`resolvePlayerSlotState` helpers) reusable by the new full-loadout tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "ship at maximum" means the six-slot loadout is full**, not a level cap. `resolvePlayerSlotState(...).isFull` is the shared authority; Extra Life / Mystery UFO never count because they are `availableWhenSlotsFull` (`AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM`).
- **Assumption — Q9's discrete-cap rule is vacuously satisfied for a power-up with no discrete variables**, so such a row is never disabled (continuous variables stay clickable, per the producer's answer). Recorded so a future reviewer does not read the "never disabled" behaviour as a bug.
- **Risk — a new `PowerUpLevelStore.remove(id)` seam could be misused by shipped gameplay.** Mitigation: document it as a gym/setup-layer operation, keep it a pure model clear with no gameplay-specific side effects, and leave the shipped `PlayScene` unchanged.
- **Risk — consumable ownership sits in `_owned` while levels sit in `_permanentGrants`**, so an incomplete removal seam would leave a "removed" consumable still owning its slot. Mitigation: AC3/AC6 require the whole-kind clear and a test asserting the slot count drops after removal.
- **Risk — the readout panel is plain DOM and the button could double-fire** (e.g. a click also toggling the collapsible header). Mitigation: append the button inside the row (inside the panel body, not the header) and cover it with a test that a single click changes the level by exactly one.
- **Risk — seeded `sceneRng()` may be unset outside a captured setup**, producing a non-reproducible victim. Mitigation: document that a seeded capture fixes the victim; the deterministic assertion uses a seeded harness.
- **Scope-creep risk** — the button could tempt extra features (undo, bulk-level, per-stat controls, persistence). Those stay **out of scope**; record any that are wanted as linked follow-up work items rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR` — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (completed; the parent of this gym).
- `AH-0MV7QKEEO006WFI1` — power-up leveling demonstration child (completed).
- `AH-0MVD1RIH2008YCNV` — Arena resolves hold-full upgrade choices through the shared choice flow (completed; the `applyMineralChoiceReward` / `grantPermanentPowerUp` seam this item reuses).
- `AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW` — consumable charge model (the "a grant is a charge, never a level" rule that Q6 = B preserves).
- `AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF` — six-slot loadout gate (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`; the "ship at maximum" condition).
- `AH-0MV5CLW6005VF7K` — the registry's single run-scoped level store (no double-count).
- `AH-0MW10ZVLH005IJRM` — Extra Life is field-pickup-only and exempt from the slot cap (why exempt kinds are never removal victims).
- `AH-0MVVJRRN10038VFR` — HUD slot classification predicate.
- `AH-0MVRMHYJR000Y9H8` — scripted-scene setup / seeded determinism (the `sceneRng` seeding the random victim).
- `AH-0MUVRACE9001WVT2` — no duplicate base/level candidate pair for the same power-up.
- `AH-0MW6OGSJP007K9W6` — red/gold mineral rotation (hold-full demonstration cadence in the same gym).
- `AH-0MV82IAYG000WS8B` — recharge-time overrides (adjacent store seam).
- `AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1` — gym↔game parity convention.
- `AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y` — owned-loadout panel in the hold-full overlay.
- `AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9` — hold-full offers level-ups only for permanently owned power-ups.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Does "assign the powerup to the player" add a new kind or only level an owned one?**
  - Answer (producer): "Don't level up on initial assignment, just add a new power-up if not already owned; if already owned then level up." Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2: Is the level increase permanent or temporary?**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — permanent (for the rest of the run, like mineral-choice grants). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: When the ship is at maximum, what is removed?**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — a random power-up kind from the player's current 6-slot loadout. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4: Button placement?**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — every power-up row in the readout panel gets its own Assign button. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5: What happens to the removed kind's accumulated levels?**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — levels are lost (the kind is removed from the loadout entirely). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q6: For consumables, does the manual button raise the level or follow the hold-full rule?**
  - Answer (producer): **B** — follow the existing hold-full rule (first assign grants ownership; repeats add a charge, not a level). Research: `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, true)` adds a charge and marks a consumable owned, never a level (`AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW` AC1). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q7: How is the random removal victim chosen?**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — drawn only from slot-counted kinds (exempt Extra Life / Mystery UFO excluded), using the gym's seeded `sceneRng()` so captures are reproducible. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q8: What does the Assign button do once the kind is at the resolver's curve cap?**
  - Answer (producer): **B** — disabled / no-op at the cap. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q9: How is "at the resolver's curve cap" decided, given the curve is asymptotic and levels are unbounded?**
  - Answer (producer): **C** — discrete variables reaching `cap` is enough; continuous variables stay clickable. Research: `curveValue` (`src/utils/curve.ts`) rounds and clamps a discrete variable at `cap`, while a continuous variable only asymptotes to it; `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` documents "levels are unbounded above". Documented consequence: a power-up with **no** discrete variables has nothing to check and stays enabled. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q10: When does a consumable's Assign button disable?**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — when its level-derived charge pool is full, or a single-use kind (Phase Shift / Teleport) already holds its ready activation (Q8's cap rule applied to the charge/readiness model). Research: `consumableCharges` / `consumableChargeCap` / `hasSingleUse` on the store. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q11: On removal, clear only the permanent level or the whole kind?**
  - Answer (producer): as recommended — clear the whole kind (permanent level, temporary stacks, consumable charges) so the slot genuinely frees. Source: interactive reply.

- **Open question (deferred, low risk):** none.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)
- **AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4** – Power ups need to be larger (completed)
- **AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X** – Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene (completed)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, already, assign, assigned, attempt (+20 more)
- `README.md` — matched: add, already, assign, assigned, attempt (+19 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: add, already, assign, attempt, gym (+17 more)

data.description:
# Hangar War needs a restart button

Add a `⟲ RESTART WAR` row to the hangar screen that returns the hangar-war payload to its
documented starting position behind a two-step confirm, keeping the all-time best score
and starting a genuinely new war.

## Problem statement

The Hangar War persists every scrap of campaign progress — hangar ownership, banked
salvage, the hex ring and the frontier aggression clock — in one `ai_hell_hangar_war`
payload with no way back to a fresh war. A player who has painted themselves into a
corner (spent salvage on the wrong hull, left a ring half-held, let aggression climb)
must clear browser storage by hand to start again, which is invisible to a player and
hostile to testers.

## Users

- **Player** — "I want to start the war over from scratch without editing browser
  storage, so I can try a different hull/weapon line after a bad run of choices."
- **Playtester / capture-tooling operator** — "I want one in-game control that returns
  the war to its documented starting position so every capture starts from the same
  state."
- **Attract-mode traversal** — must keep working unchanged: the restart control must
  never be selected by the bot, so the demo cannot stall or reset the war.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The hangar screen presents a single `⟲ RESTART WAR` row, built by the shared
   `buildHangarScreenModel` and rendered by the shared `renderHangarScreen` (so
   `HangarScene` and the read-only `GymHangar` show the same row from the same model, the
   gym reporting it non-actionable), placed after the existing `▶ DEPLOY` and `⌗ HEX MAP`
   rows (its own bottom-row slot, so no existing row moves); every existing row, label,
   colour and focus-order entry is unchanged.
2. Activating the row **arms** it (`⚠ PRESS AGAIN TO CONFIRM`) and changes nothing else;
   the armed state auto-reverts to the idle label after an exported timeout constant, and
   is disarmed by focusing/activating any other row or leaving the screen, so a single
   stray Enter can never reset the war.
3. Activating the row a second time inside the confirm window resets the war to its
   documented starting position — the hangar back to its starting kit (basic hull, starter
   weapon owned but **not equipped**, no modifiers, 0 minerals, 0 cores, empty loadout),
   the ring back to `ringIndex` 1 with no hexes, `pendingAttacks` empty and `frontierTick`
   0 — with a **fresh random seed**, **preserving `bestScore`**, and persists the result
   immediately through `hangarWarStore` using the scene's injected storage adapter
   (no write at all when the scene runs as the attract demo).
4. A reset leaves the arcade checkpoint (`ai_hell_checkpoint`), the leaderboard
   (`ai_hell_leaderboard`) and the settings (`ai_hell_settings`) keys completely
   untouched, demonstrated by a test over an in-memory storage fake.
5. Tests cover the pure reset updater (starting-position defaults, `bestScore`
   preservation, fresh seed, non-mutation of its input), the pure two-step confirm state
   machine (arm → confirm resets, arm → timeout disarms, arm → other focus disarms), and
   both scene input paths (keyboard Enter/Space and pointer click); existing hangar
   screen and scene tests continue to pass unchanged.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change — GDD §8.2 (hangar UI
   surface), the `GymHangar` row of `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and the module/handler JSDoc —
   and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

A player can wipe a mis-spent war back to its starting position from inside the hangar,
with one deliberate two-step confirmation, instead of clearing browser storage by hand.

## Constraints

- **One screen code path (gym↔game parity).** The row must come from the shared
  `buildHangarScreenModel`/`renderHangarScreen` pair so `GymHangar` cannot drift; the gym
  renders it read-only exactly as it does every other row.
- **No purchase/reset rule in scene code.** The reset is a pure updater next to the
  existing `purchaseHangarEntry`/`equipHangarHull`/`toggleHangarWeapon`/
  `toggleHangarModifier` siblings, returning a fresh payload; the scene only persists it.
- **Destructive action needs two deliberate inputs** (operator decision, Q1 = a).
- **`bestScore` survives the reset** (operator decision, Q2 = b); everything else in the
  hangar-war payload is wiped.
- **A reset starts a genuinely new war** — fresh random seed from the shared
  `randomSeed()` (operator decision, Q3 = a); tests inject a fixed seed.
- **Attract mode must not reset.** The demo persists nothing today; the restart row must
  likewise perform no store write under `demo`, and the bot's decision function
  (`hangarAttractDecision`/`decideHangarAction`) must not gain a restart branch.
- Payload schema is unchanged (no version bump): the reset only refills the existing v1
  shape.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Bottom-row layout collision (assumed manageable).** DEPLOY sits at `GAME_HEIGHT - 52`
  and HEX MAP at `- 74` on a 540 px screen; a third row needs a `- 96` slot. Assumed to fit
  above the unlock tree; if it does not, the layout constants move and a layout assertion
  pins the spacing.
- **Armed state must live in the scene, not the row.** Every activation rebuilds the
  screen (`build()` destroys and re-creates rows), so the arm flag and its timer belong to
  `HangarScene`; resetting them on rebuild keeps the two-step semantics intact.
- **Double activation is the intended confirm.** A second pointer click on the armed row
  confirms, so the arm step must be driven by a genuine activation event and not a
  lingering timer; the exported timeout constant (with fake timers in tests) pins the
  behaviour.
- **Demo must never persist or reset.** The bot's decision function gains no restart
  branch; under `demo` the handler must not write to the store, matching the existing
  "a demo is not progress" rule.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Extending the control to the hex map, adding "reset to last
  checkpoint", or adding a seed picker are out of scope; record them as separate work
  items if they surface.
- **Assumption:** the payload schema is unchanged, so no version bump and no migration is
  needed — a reset writes the existing v1 shape.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — the shipped hangar scene: renders the model, wires
  `onBuy`/`onEquipHull`/`onToggleWeapon`/`onToggleModifier`/`onDeploy`/`onOpenMap`, persists
  through `saveHangarWarPayload`, and no-ops persistence in demo mode.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — the pure model (`buildHangarScreenModel`,
  rows, focus order) and the one renderer; already exports the `⌗ HEX MAP` navigation row
  and the pure payload updaters the reset sibling will sit beside.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `createDefaultPayload(seed)` is the
  documented starting position, `saveHangarWarPayload`/`clearHangarWarPayload` already
  exist, and the `ai_hell_hangar_war` key is the only war state.
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` and `normaliseSeed()` for the fresh war seed.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — renders the same model read-only (no handlers), so it
  picks the new row up automatically as non-actionable.
- `src/core/featureFlags.ts` — the `hangarWar` flag (ON by default) gates the whole flow,
  so no extra gating is needed for the control.

## Desired change

A `⟲ RESTART WAR` row on the hangar screen, armed by a first activation and committed by
a second, that replaces the current payload with `createDefaultPayload(randomSeed())` and
carries the previous `bestScore` forward. One pure updater
(`restartHangarWar(payload, seed)`) implements the rule; the screen model gains a
`restartRow` plus its confirm-state presentation; `HangarScene` gains an `onRestart`
handler (and the arm/confirm timer) that persists the fresh payload.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — add `HangarRestartRow`, `restartRow` on the
  model, the confirm/idle label helper, `onRestart` handler, layout slot for the row, and
  the pure `restartHangarWar` updater beside the existing updaters.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — wire `onRestart`, own the arming/confirm state and its
  timer, persist the fresh payload, keep demo persistence off.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — reuse `createDefaultPayload`; add a small
  `restartPayload(payload, seed)` helper (or keep it in the screen module) that preserves
  `bestScore`.
- `src/core/rng.ts` — reuse `randomSeed()` for the new war seed.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` — model, updater, confirm state machine and scene
  input-path tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` — assert the restart row renders non-actionable.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — document the row and the
  reset rule.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — capture-tooling note for the new hangar row.

## Related work

### Related work items

- AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE — Build Candidate D — Hangar War (outer loop): the parent build of
  the hangar slice and the first hex ring; defines the starting war this control returns to.
- AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1 — Hangar scene: unlock tree and deployment/loadout selector (the
  screen the row is added to).
- AH-0MVUXC0M5007LCGV — Versioned `ai_hell_hangar_war` store with migration (the payload
  and its defaults).
- AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP — Gate Hangar War behind a feature flag (why no extra gating is
  needed). *(automated related-work match)*
- AH-0MVUXCC5J0028OGQ — Docs: Hangar War specification, build status and parity record
  (the docs to extend).
- AH-0MTV7OAJM002GGMM — Move control buttons for gym scenes to the bottom *(automated
  related-work match)*: the convention this bottom-row placement should follow.
- AH-0MU9KSFMQ005SAT1 — When a game restarts all existing power-ups should be cleared
  *(automated related-work match)*: precedent for restart/reset semantics; this item is
  about in-run power-ups, not the persisted war, so it is reference only and not a
  dependency.

### Related docs and files

- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (persistence and save model) — design of
  record for what a war consists of.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — the hangar UI surface to extend.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the `GymHangar` row that must name the new row.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — capture-tooling notes; the new row may need a line so
  the capture bot's hangar traversal stays accurate. *(automated file match)*

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the restart be a single press or a two-step confirmation?" — Options:
  (a) two-step in-place confirm, (b) immediate, (c) separate confirmation sub-screen.
  — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **(a) two-step in-place confirm** — the reset
  wipes all war progress and a second deliberate press prevents accidental loss.
- Q: "What exactly does the reset wipe?" — Options: (a) everything in the hangar-war
  payload including `bestScore`, (b) everything except `bestScore`, (c) hangar + ring
  only. — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **(b) everything except `bestScore`** —
  the all-time hangar-war record is kept; hangar ownership/loadout, banked salvage, ring,
  pending attacks and the frontier clock return to the starting position. Research:
  `HangarWarPayload` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts:108`) confirms those are exactly the
  fields of the war payload; checkpoint/leaderboard/settings are separate keys, so they
  are untouched by construction.
- Q: "What seed does the fresh war get?" — Options: (a) fresh random seed, (b) reuse the
  current seed, (c) always the default seed 0. — Answer (operator, interactive reply):
  **(a) fresh random seed** — a restart should produce a genuinely new war; tests inject a
  fixed seed through the existing injectable-storage/payload seams. Research:
  `randomSeed()` already exists in `src/core/rng.ts:49` and `createDefaultPayload(seed)`
  normalises it.

Parent: AH-0MVHWG20L002EOR1 (re-scope). First child of the test-layout alignment; blocks C2–C6.

## Goal
Introduce the infrastructure the later migration children depend on, without moving any test yet:
- add a `@/*` → `src/*` TypeScript/Vite/Vitest path alias;
- make `tests/` a recognised test root and include `tests/**/*.ts` in tsconfig;
- teach the Vitest classifier (`vitest.projects.ts`) to resolve `@/` imports when walking transitive imports (otherwise Phaser/DOM detection breaks once tests use the alias).

## Acceptance criteria
1. `tsconfig.json` maps `@/*` to `src/*` (`paths: { "@/*": ["./src/*"] }` — TypeScript 7 removed `baseUrl`, so the relative form is used) and `include` contains `tests`.
2. `vite.config.ts` and `vitest.config.ts` resolve `@/*` to `src/*` (Vitest projects inherit it).
3. `vitest.projects.ts` resolves `@/x` specifiers to `src/x` during transitive Phaser/DOM analysis; a unit test pins this.
4. `TEST_ROOTS` includes `tests` and `TEST_INCLUDE_GLOBS` includes `tests/**/*.test.ts`.
5. `npm run typecheck` passes and the existing `unit` project is green (no behaviour change).
6. The vitest config documents the alias + `tests/` root.

## Files
- tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts, vitest.config.ts, vitest.projects.ts
- src/test/projectMembership.test.ts (extend) or a new classifier test

## Notes
No test relocation in this child; moving starts in C2/C3/C4.


## Impact
Contributors can now import game modules via a single `@/` alias in both app and test code, and the suite is ready to move into the standard top-level `tests/` tree without changing which tests run in the fast node project versus the Phaser/happy-dom project.

Pre-existing bug discovered during real-browser verification of AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ (AH-0MVWIDPWH005VB9Z, AC6, discovered-from:AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ).

## Problem
scripts/record-session.mjs --bot presses Tab → Enter to start the in-game demo, but the menu's FocusManager control order is now Play Game (focused by default) → Hangar War → Watch Demo → Settings (Hangar War ships ON). One Tab lands on Hangar War and Enter opens HangarScene, so a --bot recording captures 0 telemetry records (real headless reproduction: exit 0, Records: 0, empty file). This silently defeats the tool's primary ghost-recording use case.

## Evidence (real headless runs, this worktree)
- node scripts/record-session.mjs --headless --bot --seed 12345 --auto --max-duration 60000 → Records: 0, exit 0, smoke-a.jsonl empty.
- Same without --auto, Ctrl+C after 12 s → Records: 0, exit 0, empty file.
- scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs uses Tab → Tab → Enter for the demo (captureStartKeys('demo'), AH-0MUXVVYWY009WT3X — back-to-back keys race focus changes, 250 ms gap), which is the working sequence.

## Expected behaviour
--bot records the demo run: either Tab → Tab → Enter with the 250 ms gap (mirroring capture), or the demo button is focused directly. Should be covered by a real/browser-level check (the hermetic tests inject page/fs and cannot catch a menu-layout drift like this).

## Acceptance criteria
1. A real headless node scripts/record-session.mjs --headless --bot --seed N --auto run produces a non-empty recording whose records include a run_header for seed N (exit 0).
2. The fix reuses capture-gameplay's demo start plan or otherwise stays stable against menu layout changes (a test or invariant documents the dependency).
3. Full project test suite passes with the change.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL** – Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (completed)
- **AH-0MVWMUQUC003WXF5** – Ensure bot navigates Hangar War screens for npm run capture (completed)
- **AH-0MUXVVYWY009WT3X** – Capture demo start is flaky: Tab and Enter dispatched too close together (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, auto, back, behaviour, bot (+110 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvvh57ll00038wq, ac6, acceptance, auto, back (+107 more)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: ac6, acceptance, auto, back, behaviour (+105 more)

## Implementation notes (plan review)

**Root cause confirmed in code:** `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` registers its menu controls in visual order — `playButton` → `hangarWarButton` → `demoButton` → `settingsButton` (MenuScene.ts ~645-670) — so from the default `Play Game` focus one **Tab** lands on `🛠  Hangar War`, and **Enter** starts `HangarScene`. `scripts/record-session.mjs` (~754-760) presses exactly `Tab` → `Enter` for `--bot`. `HangarScene` has no run-end signal, so `--auto` runs to `--max-duration` and the recording ends with 0 records.

**Fix sketch (smallest end-to-end slice):**
- Replace the inline `Tab` → `Enter` with the shared start plan already exported by `capture-gameplay.mjs`: `captureStartPlan('demo')` yields `Tab` → 250 ms → `Tab` → 250 ms → `Enter`, which `captureStartKeys('demo')` / `captureStartPlan` encode and `capture-gameplay.test.ts` already pins (AH-0MUXVVYWY009WT3X, AH-0MVWMUQUC003WXF5). `record-session.mjs` already imports several helpers from that module, so this adds no new dependency.
- Drop the local `START_KEY_GAP_MS` duplicate (record-session.mjs ~line 71) in favour of the shared constant, so the recorder and the capture tool cannot drift apart again.
- Extract a testable seam (e.g. `startRecordingRun({ pressKey, wait, mode })`, dependency-injected like the existing `runRecordingWaitLoop` / `createRecordingCheckpoint` seams) so a hermetic unit test can assert the demo sequence is exactly `captureStartPlan('demo')` with 250 ms gaps, and that the human path is still a single `Enter`.
- Optional hardening (only if it stays cheap): assert the expected scene is active before recording, as `npm run capture` does through the dev-gated director, so a future menu-layout drift fails loudly instead of silently recording nothing.
- Optional hardening: seed the Hangar War flag ON before boot (`installHangarWarFlag(buildHangarWarFlagPlan())`, as the `--hangar` capture path already does) so the two-Tab path does not rely on the shipped default flag value. `record-session` opens a fresh non-persistent Chromium context today, so the shipped default (`hangarWar: true`) applies — robustness note, not a current defect.
- Docs: the `--bot` row in `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` already says "Watch Demo", so no change is strictly required; if the fix introduces a shared-plan seam worth naming, add one line next to the demo start-key description in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.

**Test-first order:** (1) hermetic test pinning the recorder's start plan to `captureStartPlan('demo')` — it fails against today's `Tab` → `Enter`; (2) the implementation that reuses the shared plan; (3) the real headless verification run that satisfies AC1.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/record-session.mjs`
- `scripts/record-session.test.ts`
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts`
- `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`


## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (plan)

No producer questions were asked: the pre-check returned `decision: skip` (effort Small / risk Low), and the description already carried a reproduction, evidence, expected behaviour and testable ACs, so the auto-complete review path ran instead of an interview.

- Q: "Is this a duplicate of the completed capture-tool fixes (AH-0MUXVVYWY009WT3X, AH-0MVWMUQUC003WXF5)?" — Answer (plan, self-resolved): no. Those fixed `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`'s start gesture; `record-session.mjs` keeps its own inline `Tab` → `Enter` and was never covered. Evidence: `grep` of `captureStartKeys`/`startPlan` shows no `record-session` consumer, and `scripts/record-session.test.ts` has no start-gesture test.
- Q: "Does the documented menu order still match the shipped code?" — Answer (plan, resolved from source): yes. `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` (~645-670) registers `playButton` → `hangarWarButton` → `demoButton` → `settingsButton`, and `hangarWar` defaults ON (`src/core/featureFlags.ts`), so one Tab still lands on Hangar War.
- **OPEN QUESTION (directed to the producer, non-blocking):** include the optional scene-activation assertion (fail loudly on menu drift) in this fix, or leave it out to keep the change minimal? Recorded rather than assumed; the plan's default is to leave it out.
- Assumption recorded (not asked): `record-session` opens a fresh non-persistent Chromium context, so `hangarWar` resolves to its shipped default (ON) and the two-Tab demo path is deterministic. If a persisted profile is ever introduced, the fix must seed the flag (`installHangarWarFlag(buildHangarWarFlagPlan())`).

## Impact

`--bot` now correctly starts the in-game demo for ghost-recording, instead of opening Hangar War on a single Tab press.
