# Repeated gameplay pauses in later stages and mini-boss — dev telemetry uploader stalls frames and floods errors (AH-0MWDFAJAC005R3NI)

## Problem statement

During play in dev mode the game repeatedly pauses — most noticeably in the later stages and the mini-boss stage — while the console floods with dev-telemetry errors (`dev upload skipped after an error: RangeError: Invalid string length` in `linesToNdjson`, and `run-end upload skipped: N MiB … over the 8.0 MiB upload cap` with N growing monotonically to 280+ MiB across a session). Source inspection shows the dev streaming uploader serialises the **entire unconfirmed buffer** synchronously on the main thread inside the frame loop; because uploads keep failing, the buffer never drains, so each later attempt re-pays the whole serialisation + `Array.join` cost — the observed 135–139 ms `requestAnimationFrame` handler violations.

## Users

- **Developer/operator running `npm run dev` and demo runs** — playtesting the game through late stages and the mini-boss while dev telemetry collection is on by default.
- **Perf engineers** — measuring frame time with the dev recorder enabled must measure the game, not the recorder.

User story: *As a developer playtesting in dev mode, I want the telemetry machinery to stay out of the frame and keep its buffer bounded, so the game plays smoothly through late stages and the mini-boss and the console stays readable.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- The dev streaming uploader never builds a part by serialising the whole unconfirmed buffer in one synchronous operation — a multi-hundred-MiB backlog cannot reach `linesToNdjson`'s `Array.join` and cannot raise `RangeError: Invalid string length` or stall the main thread (unit test at the part-building seam, plus assertion that no couple-of-hundreds-of-ms RAF violations occur in a dev demo run).
- The in-memory telemetry backlog stops growing unboundedly across a session: content already confirmed by the dev server (or finally skipped as over-cap) is no longer re-read and re-serialised by later run-end uploads — a run-end upload of a long session no longer re-pays the whole-buffer serialise+redact cost (test on the read/drain seam; the dev CLI tooling accessor keeps its guarantees).
- The console spam stops: a failed/skipped dev upload is reported once per part/run (coalesced into the existing backoff window), not repeatedly from the frame loop; over-cap parts are reported once, not per attempt.
- Redaction guarantees stay intact: no unredacted payload is ever written to a sink; the existing redaction tests still pass unchanged.
- The headless frame-time harness (`scripts/measure-performance.mjs`, docs/PERFORMANCE.md) shows no regression in late-game p95/FPS with the dev recorder enabled, and the measured telemetry bucket share is materially lower than the current ~5 % of JS (before/after numbers recorded on this item).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, docs/TELEMETRY.md, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can play through the late stages and the mini-boss with smooth frames and a readable console instead of hitches that get worse the longer the run goes.

## Constraints

- **Dev-only scope** (confirmed by operator): production telemetry (opt-in remote sink) is untouched.
- **Redaction invariant**: no unredacted payload may reach any sink — the size-guard/drain changes must not create a path that skips redaction for a written payload.
- **Buffer retention contract**: the dev sink's buffer is intentionally retained for the run-end upload and the dev CLI/`window.__aiHellTelemetry` tooling — draining must not break those consumers or the streaming part protocol (confirmed offsets).
- The dev telemetry streamer's part protocol (confirmed-offset watermark, exactly-once resend-on-gap, backoff) must keep working for the happy path.

## Existing state

- `JsonlTelemetrySink` (`src/telemetry/sinks.ts`) serialises every record to a line and never clears or rewrites its in-memory buffer; `read()` returns the entire NDJSON string.
- The streaming uploader (`src/telemetry/devStream.ts`) `pendingRange()` calls `readBuffer()` → `splitNdjsonLines` → `linesToNdjson` (a single `Array.join` across all pending lines) synchronously per attempt, triggered from the batch observer → `streamer.push()` chain that runs inside the Phaser update step.
- The run-end whole-file uploader (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` ~5665–5674) re-reads the whole buffer and re-serialises it every run end.
- Uploads fail (8 MiB cap skip; `RangeError` once the joined string exceeds V8's string-length limit), so the buffer never drains and grows unboundedly across a session.
- AH-0MW2DC20A007TAVY (open) documents the ~5 % of JS serialisation cost with the same over-cap-discard root cause; kept open and cross-linked per operator decision.

## Desired change

- Make the streaming uploader operate on a **bounded window** (by record count and/or byte budget) rather than the whole unconfirmed buffer, so a large backlog is split into sizeable parts and can never produce a main-thread stall or `RangeError`; keep the confirmed-offset watermark semantics.
- Bound/drain the retained buffer so a session's backlog cannot grow without limit and run-end uploads stop re-serialising the entire history (e.g. discard confirmed/skipped content, cap retained bytes, or have the run-end upload reuse the streamer's part accounting).
- Ensure a failed/skipped attempt is not re-reported from the frame loop — reuse the existing backoff coalescing so a mid-run failure reports once.
- Keep dev CLI tooling and the dev-gated `window.__aiHellTelemetry` accessor working.

## Key Files

- `src/telemetry/devStream.ts` — `pendingRange`/`attemptPart`/`sendPart`: bound per-attempt serialisation window; honour existing backoff.
- `src/telemetry/devStreamProtocol.ts` — `splitNdjsonLines`/`nextPartRange`: window splitting that avoids whole-buffer joins.
- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` — `linesToNdjson` (join cost) and the buffer retention/drain policy.
- `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` / `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — `readBuffer`/flush seams the streamer and run-end uploader share.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — run-end whole-file uploader (~5665–5674) and streaming-observer wiring (~6529–6575).
- Tests: `src/telemetry/devStream.test.ts`, `devUpload.test.ts`, `sinks.test.ts`, `devStreamProtocol.test.ts`, `PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/TELEMETRY.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Drain/discard risk:** draining confirmed (or finally-skipped) content must not break the streaming part protocol (confirmed-offset watermark, exactly-once resend on gap) or the dev CLI tooling / `window.__aiHellTelemetry` accessor. Mitigation: keep the watermark semantics and cover the drain seam with the existing devStream/protocol tests.
- **Part-sizing risk:** bounding the per-attempt window changes part sizes; the dev server's confirmed-count protocol must stay compatible (part-protocol tests exist to guard this).
- **RangeError guard assumption:** a bounded per-part byte budget (well under V8's max string length) replaces the current unbounded `Array.join`; a guard test asserts a large backlog cannot reach `linesToNdjson` with an oversized pending range.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any further frame-loop optimisation outside the telemetry path is out of scope — track separately (relevant items exist, e.g. AH-0MW2DC28M00161W6).
- Assumption: dev-only bug; production telemetry (opt-in remote sink) is out of scope and untouched.

## Related work

- AH-0MW2DC20A007TAVY — *Dev telemetry serialisation costs ~5 % of JS during demo runs* (open, idea): overlapping root fix for the over-cap serialise-then-discard cost; intentionally kept separate and cross-linked (operator decision); the frame-loop jank, unbounded buffer growth, and spam are this item's scope.
- AH-0MW2DC28M00161W6 (open) — *Attract-mode demo bot steering is the top game-code cost in late-game PlayScene*: separate late-game cost, out of scope here but worth excluding in measurements.
- AH-0MVNT25JI004OVKQ / AH-0MVNVGP55002G0KH (completed) — prior diagnosis: dev telemetry upload overflowing the CDP pipe (single >512 MiB message).
- AH-0MVXV0F0Y004NENT (completed) — *Remove per-frame allocations from the PlayScene hot loop*.
- AH-0MVXV0DER009ER70 (completed) — *Frame-time performance harness for PlayScene*; docs/PERFORMANCE.md.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where does this happen — dev mode only, or production builds too?" — Answer (operator): "Only tested in dev mode." Source: interactive reply. Recorded: dev-only scope; production telemetry out of scope.
- Q2: "Desired outcome for the fix?" — Answer (operator): "Option A — make the dev telemetry machinery stop blocking the frame loop, stop accumulating unboundedly, and stop the error spam." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Relationship to the open item AH-0MW2DC20A007TAVY (dev telemetry serialisation ~5 % of JS)?" — Answer (operator): "Option A — keep both items, cross-linked." Source: interactive reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD** – Crash resilience: incremental telemetry upload so a mid-run reload loses at most one batch (completed)
- **AH-0MVBMRK6X0069QDI** – Game-side uploader fired at run end (completed)
- **AH-0MW6NFRQR0062D90** – Part-protocol contract and hermetic tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvxv0der009er70, acceptance, accessor, accounting, accumulating (+290 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: acceptance, accessor, accounting, already, answer (+288 more)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: 0mvnt25ji004ovkq, 0mvnvgp55002g0kh, 0mvxv0der009er70, acceptance, accessor (+279 more)

## Goal

Hermetic **test-first gate** for AH-0MWDFAJAC005R3NI: pin the new telemetry-seam contracts with red tests before the implementation slices land (same repo pattern the original part protocol used — "pinned by hermetic tests before the streaming wiring lands"). **This item changes no production code.**

The seams under test (implemented by the F3 and F2 children):

- **Protocol window splitting** — the pending-range reader splits a large unconfirmed backlog into bounded windows (a byte budget ~2 MiB, mirroring `TELEMETRY_READ_CHUNK_CHARS`, plus a record ceiling) so `linesToNdjson` never joins an oversized window.
- **Drain seam** — `createMemoryLineWriter` gains a bounded-retention cap (drop oldest confirmed/skipped first), with base-offset bookkeeping so absolute record counts stay correct and only the unconfirmed pending range is re-read.
- **Deferral seam** — the streamer's part build+send is deferred off the gameplay frame task through an injectable scheduler (synchronous in hermetic tests), and a part-build failure routes through the existing backoff window (reported once, not per frame-loop trigger).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test at the part-building seam proves a multi-hundred-MiB backlog can never reach `linesToNdjson`'s `Array.join`: every pending-range window is bounded by a byte budget and a record ceiling, so `RangeError: Invalid string length` is unreachable.
- A test on the read/drain seam proves confirmed (or finally-skipped) content is no longer re-read and re-serialised: the retained buffer is bounded and the windowed read returns only the unconfirmed, in-order window with correct absolute offsets.
- A hermetic test proves a failed/skipped part is reported once per part/run (coalesced into the existing backoff window), not repeatedly from the frame-loop trigger, and an over-cap part is reported once.
- The seam signatures these tests target are exactly the ones the F3/F2 implementation children implement; the tests are the red half of the test-first gate and pass unchanged once the implementation lands.
- The streaming part-protocol happy path (confirmed-offset watermark, exactly-once resend-on-gap, backoff) stays pinned by the existing devStream/protocol tests, which keep passing.

## Key Files

- `src/telemetry/devStreamProtocol.test.ts` — window-splitting guard tests
- `src/telemetry/sinks.test.ts` — drain-seam/retention-cap tests
- `src/telemetry/devStream.test.ts` — deferral-seam and report-once tests
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md` — loss-bound and offline behaviour the new seams change

## Impact

Developers playtesting in dev mode can finish a long run through the late stages and the mini-boss without frame hitches, a growing memory backlog or a console flooded with telemetry errors — the seam contracts this item pins (bounded part windows, retention-bounded drain, off-frame deferral) are the test-first gate that lets the implementation land safely.

data.description:
## Goal

Bound the dev JSONL sink's retained in-memory buffer and expose a **windowed read/drain seam** so uploaders stop re-reading and re-serialising the whole run (AH-0MWDFAJAC005R3NI, AC2/AC4).

- `createMemoryLineWriter` (`src/telemetry/sinks.ts`) gains a bounded-retention policy: a configurable cap (`VITE_TELEMETRY_MAX_RETAINED_MESSAGE_BYTES`, default 16 MiB) on retained line bytes; once over the cap the buffer drops the **oldest** records first — already-confirmed (or finally-skipped) content preferred, oldest unconfirmed dropped only as the final bound so memory stays bounded even under a total dev-server outage. The writer tracks a dropped-record base so absolute record-count offsets stay correct (a drain can never break the confirmed-offset watermark semantics).
- Expose through `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` / `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` as a windowed read/drain seam: the streamer reads only the pending window from an absolute record offset — no whole-buffer `linesToNdjson` re-join on the streamer or run-end path.
- `window.__aiHellTelemetry` (and the capture/record chunked readers) keep returning the whole **retained** run: normal demo runs (measured 0.67–4 MiB) are byte-identical because the cap is far above their size; multi-hour sessions stay bounded.
- The whole-file run-end fallback (no streamer loaded) stays size-guarded and is additionally bounded by the cap.
- Update `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` / `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` and the `devStreamDocs.test.ts` assertions from "never cleared" to the bounded-retention contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The in-memory telemetry backlog stops growing unboundedly across a session: the retained buffer is bounded by the retention cap (drop-oldest-confirmed-first, oldest unconfirmed only as the final bound), verified by a test on the read/drain seam.
- Content already confirmed by the dev server (or finally skipped as over-cap) is no longer re-read and re-serialised by later run-end uploads: the windowed read returns only the unconfirmed pending range without re-joining the whole buffer.
- The dev CLI tooling accessor keeps its guarantees: `window.__aiHellTelemetry.read()` returns the whole retained run and is byte-identical to today for a normal-sized run (below the cap); the capture/record chunked readers are unaffected.
- Redaction guarantees stay intact: no unredacted payload is ever written to a sink; the existing redaction tests pass unchanged.
- The streaming part protocol (confirmed-offset watermark, exactly-once resend-on-gap, backoff) keeps working for the happy path with the new seam; existing devStream/protocol tests still pass.

## Key Files

- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` — `createMemoryLineWriter` retention cap + windowed read seam
- `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` / `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — readBuffer/flush seams
- `src/telemetry/sinks.test.ts` — drain-seam tests
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`, `src/telemetry/devStreamDocs.test.ts` — bounded-retention contract
## Impact

Developers playtesting in dev mode can run multi-hour sessions with a bounded telemetry backlog instead of an ever-growing buffer, while every normal demo run is still captured byte-identically to before.

data.description:
## Goal

Make the dev streaming uploader build every part from a **bounded window** and run **off the gameplay frame task**, so a multi-hundred-MiB backlog can never stall frames or raise `RangeError: Invalid string length` (AH-0MWDFAJAC005R3NI, AC1/AC3).

- `src/telemetry/devStreamProtocol.ts`: the pending-range reader splits the unconfirmed backlog into bounded windows — a byte budget (~2 MiB of body, mirroring the CDP-safe chunk size) plus a record ceiling (e.g. 4096) — so `linesToNdjson` never joins an oversized window. Uses the F3 windowed read/drain seam (absolute record offsets, no whole-buffer re-join).
- `src/telemetry/devStream.ts`: `pendingRange`/`attemptPart` build each part from one bounded window; `finalise()` drains a backlog in chained non-final parts followed by the single `final: true` part; happy path unchanged (one ≤ batch-size part per flush, in flush order, chained one at a time; exactly-once watermark, gap re-sync and backoff semantics preserved).
- **Off-frame deferral**: part build+send runs through an injectable `defer` scheduler seam (`queueMicrotask`/`setTimeout(0)`/`requestIdleCallback` in the browser; synchronous in hermetic tests), so telemetry serialisation never runs inside the Phaser update/rAF task.
- **Report-once**: a part-build failure (including an oversized-window guard) routes through the existing `recordFailure` backoff path, so a failed/skipped upload is reported once per part/run and over-cap parts once, not from every frame-loop trigger.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` run-end keeps `streamer.finalise()` (already wired); with the F3 seam it no longer re-reads the whole buffer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The dev streaming uploader never builds a part by serialising the whole unconfirmed buffer in one synchronous operation: the pending range is split into bounded windows (byte budget + record ceiling), so a multi-hundred-MiB backlog cannot reach `linesToNdjson`'s `Array.join` or raise `RangeError: Invalid string length` (unit test at the part-building seam).
- Part build and send are deferred off the gameplay frame task via an injectable scheduler seam — the rAF/update step is never held by telemetry part work.
- The console spam stops: a failed/skipped dev upload is reported once per part/run (coalesced into the existing backoff window), not repeatedly from the frame loop; over-cap parts are reported once, not per attempt.
- Run end drains a large backlog in chained parts ending with one `final: true` part; a run-end upload of a long session no longer re-pays the whole-buffer serialise cost (reuses the windowed seam and the streamer's part accounting).
- The happy path keeps one part per flush, in flush order, with exactly-once watermark semantics; existing devStream/protocol tests still pass.

## Key Files

- `src/telemetry/devStream.ts` — `pendingRange`/`attemptPart`/`sendPart`/`finalise`, `defer` seam
- `src/telemetry/devStreamProtocol.ts` — `nextPartRange` window splitting
- `src/telemetry/devStream.test.ts`, `src/telemetry/devStreamProtocol.test.ts` — window/deferral/report-once tests
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — run-end finalise wiring (~5665)
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md` — streaming / offline-retry / cap sections

## Impact

Developers playtesting in dev mode get smooth frames and a readable console: telemetry now uploads in bounded windows scheduled off the frame task instead of serialising the whole backlog inside the update step.
